<title>Phase 3: Any-PDS rescue and migration destination — capability-gated finalize</title>
<description>
Part of <issue id="d5cb6e3d-f781-4ecb-aebf-c954915b3708" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-452/obsign-without-custos-first-class-any-pds-wallet-support-epic">MM-452</issue>. Design: `docs/design-plans/2026-07-24-obsign-without-custos.md` §Phase 3.

## Why

Recovering an account is the worst possible moment to present a hosting decision with only one viable answer. Today every leg of sovereign disaster recovery (`disaster_recovery.rs`) and outbound migration works against any PDS — offline service-auth JWT verified via [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>), standard `createAccount`/`importRepo`/`uploadBlob`/`activateAccount` — **except** the finalize: `finalize_migration_core` unconditionally mints the destination sovereign session via `/v1/sessions/sovereign`, which only Custos serves. A reference-PDS destination would die at the last step, after the identity op already landed.

## What

Branch the injected `ensure_session` step on the destination's `sovereignSessions` capability (<issue id="e2abaa52-2747-4daf-8c10-209294bd5183" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-454/phase-0b-custos-capability-extension-in-describeserver-self">MM-454</issue>):

* **Capability present (Custos):** today's behavior — mint + persist the sovereign session before deactivating the source.
* **Capability absent:** durably persist the Bearer session already held from the migration `createAccount` (via the existing `OAuthClient::new_bearer` + versioned `{did}:oauth-tokens` record) as the destination credential, preserving the strict activate → durable-credential → deactivate ordering. Post-cutover session lifecycle then rides Phase 2's password unlock path (<issue id="7d621f07-95f0-490d-a547-4f75b3e9f24c" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-457/phase-2-foreign-pds-session-provider-password-createsession-unlock">MM-457</issue>).

Same branch serves both flows for free: sovereign disaster recovery to a non-Custos destination, and normal outbound migration between two non-Custos hosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Disaster recovery rebuilds an account onto a reference PDS end-to-end from the iCloud backups, with the same abort-safety ordering (a credential-persistence failure leaves nothing half-live and is retryable).
2. Outbound migration to a non-Custos destination finalizes without ever calling `/v1/sessions/sovereign`.
3. Custos-destination behavior is byte-identical to today (existing orchestrator tests unchanged).
4. The destination-picker UI presents Custos and other-PDS destinations with equal weight — the Custos pitch is its capabilities, not the only working button.

Depends on <issue id="e2abaa52-2747-4daf-8c10-209294bd5183" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-454/phase-0b-custos-capability-extension-in-describeserver-self">MM-454</issue> (capability probe); post-cutover authenticated features on a non-Custos destination depend on <issue id="7d621f07-95f0-490d-a547-4f75b3e9f24c" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-457/phase-2-foreign-pds-session-provider-password-createsession-unlock">MM-457</issue>.
</description>

<title>Obsign without Custos — first-class any-PDS wallet support (epic)</title>
<description>
## Strategy

Broaden Obsign's market beyond Custos-hosted accounts: a user on the reference PDS, [bsky.social](<http://bsky.social>), or any spec-compliant PDS should get real, honest value from the wallet — Secure-Enclave root key, PLC monitoring + 72h override, user-held repo/media backup, self-held Shamir recovery — with Custos capabilities (escrow-assisted recovery, passwordless sovereign sessions, agents, wallet-confirmed consent) as the opt-in upgrade rather than a lock-in. Rescue and migration must never force a stressed user onto Custos.

Design doc: `docs/design-plans/2026-07-24-obsign-without-custos.md` (survey of what already works without Custos, the ecosystem describeServer survey, the capability-extension design, and phase rationale).

## As-built starting point (verified 2026-07-24, v0.8.1)

Already works on any PDS today: the claim/import flow (device key → `rotationKeys[0]` via standard lexicons), PLC monitoring + recovery override ([plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) only), repo + blob backup (public sync endpoints, no session), endpoint repair, sovereign share-based recovery (Shares 1+3), and disaster recovery **into a Custos destination**.

Custos-locked today: create ceremony, Shamir generation/re-key (fused to `/v1/dids` + escrow), sovereign sessions (and everything downstream: app passwords, change handle, removal, blob restore), agents/consent, and the rescue/migration **destination** (finalize unconditionally mints `/v1/sessions/sovereign`).

## Phases (one child issue each)

* Phase 0a — mode-select honesty: "Create an identity" / "Import an identity" + non-Custos create gate
* Phase 0b — `custos` capability extension in describeServer + self-identifying `_health`
* Phase 0c — positioning + live validation of the any-PDS arc (claim → backup → rescue)
* Phase 1 — self-held Shamir kit for foreign-hosted identities (escrow-less re-key)
* Phase 2 — foreign-PDS session provider (password `createSession` unlock path)
* Phase 3 — any-PDS rescue/migration destination (capability-gated finalize)

Parked (needs its own design pass, deliberately not in this epic): "create-then-sovereignize" — creating a brand-new account on a reference PDS via standard `createAccount` then immediately running the claim ceremony.
</description>

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

Every leg of sovereign disaster recovery and outbound migration already worked against any PDS — offline service-auth JWT verified via plc.directory, standard `createAccount`/`importRepo`/`uploadBlob`/`activateAccount` — except the finalize. `finalize_migration` minted the destination session via `/v1/sessions/sovereign`, a Custos-only route, so a reference-PDS or bsky.social destination failed at the last step, *after* the identity op had already landed.

`destination_credential` (pure, unit-tested) decides which credential the cutover persists, from the DID method plus the destination's advertised `sovereignSessions` capability:

| destination | credential |
|---|---|
| answered, advertises `sovereignSessions` | Sovereign — unchanged from today |

# Batch PR Review-Comment Triage

Pull every unresolved review thread on the current PR in one command, then triage the batch. The user should never have to paste review comments one at a time.

## Fetch unresolved threads

Determine the PR number for the current branch (`gh pr view --json number -q .number`), then:

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='
query($owner:String!,$repo:String!,$pr:Int!){
  repository(owner:$owner,name:$repo){
    pullRequest(number:$pr){
      reviewThreads(first:100){
        nodes{
          isResolved isOutdated path line
          comments(first:30){nodes{author{login} body url}}
        }
      }
    }
  }
}' -F owner=<owner> -F repo=<repo> -F pr=<number> \
| jq '[.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[]
       | select(.isResolved==false)
       | {path, line, isOutdated,
          comments: [.comments.nodes[] | {author: .author.login, url, body}]}]'
```

Also fetch top-level (non-thread) review bodies and issue comments if the bot posts summaries there:

```bash
gh pr view <number> --json reviews,comments
```

## Triage the batch

For each unresolved thread, classify before fixing anything:

1. **Correctness / security / portability** — verify the claim against the actual code, then fix if real. Automated reviewers assert confidently and are sometimes wrong; refute with evidence when they are.
2. **Legitimate but out of scope** — file a follow-up issue rather than growing the PR.
3. **Pure style nit / preference** — decline with a one-line reason.

Present the full disposition table (thread → classification → action) to the user in ONE message before applying fixes, so they approve the batch rather than each item. Note that every fix-commit re-triggers CI and (for assertive bots like CodeRabbit) a fresh review round that tends to find one more micro-nit — batch fixes into a single commit where possible.

## Resolving threads

After pushing fixes, reply/resolve via:

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='mutation($id:ID!){resolveReviewThread(input:{threadId:$id}){thread{isResolved}}}' -F id=<threadId>
```

(Include `id` in the reviewThreads query above if you plan to resolve threads programmatically.)
